ukberi-tibyan:2-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ (٢) عَامِلَةٌ نَاصِبَةٌ (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (وُجُوهٌ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خَاشِعَةٌ» is its khabar (predicate), and «يَوْمَئِذٍ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for the khabar, and «عَامِلَةٌ» is a description of them by what they were in this world.

ukberi-tibyan:23-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّى وَكَفَرَ (٢٣) فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ (٢٤) إِنَّ إِلَيْنَا إِيَابَهُمْ (٢٥)).
The words of the Exalted (إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّى): it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).
«الْإِيَابُ» (the return) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «آبَ يَؤُوبُ», like «الْقِيَامُ» and «الصِّيَامُ»; the wāw was changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it and its being weak in the verb.
It is also read with a doubled yāʾ («إِيَّابَهُمْ»); its origin is «إِيوَابٌ» on the pattern «فِيعَالٌ»; the wāw and the yāʾ came together and the first of them was preceded by sukūn [Translator's note: i.e. the first of them was vowelless], so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and assimilated.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِيعٍ (٦)).
(إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِيعٍ): it may be in the position of the accusative (naṣb) according to the basic rule of the chapter [of exception], and it may be nominative as a badal (substitute).
